abstraction_design.rationale: The shared abstractions (card list, type badge, load state, move table, byName) are sized exactly to the app's real variation, so an Items page reuses nearly everything; the residual cost is the ~60-line detail-page skeleton that gets copied per resource.

findings.issue: The static server duplicates the client's route and resource knowledge (DETAIL_ROUTES mirrors app.routes.ts; the 404-check path re-encodes what PokeApi.byName does), so adding/removing a resource page requires synchronized edits in two runtimes.
findings.suggestion: Generate the route table from a shared module (e.g. import a routes/resources list from src/app into the server build), or accept the duplication but document it in app.routes.ts next to each detail route.

findings.issue: The single global stylesheet targets component element selectors (app-load-state, app-home, app-types-page, app-move-page, and .count:has(+ app-pokemon-card-list)), so renaming components or adding a similar page silently misses or breaks styling.
findings.suggestion: Move per-component rules into component-scoped `styles` (Angular's default encapsulation), keeping only tokens and truly shared classes (.panel, .type-badge, .card-*) global.

findings.issue: The detail-page wiring (resource + syncPageTitle + errorHeading + LoadState/@if hasValue template shape) is copy-pasted across the four detail pages, so a change to loading/error presentation lands four times.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small detail-page wrapper component (heading + load-state + content projection) or a `createDetailResource` helper; or leave as-is but note the pattern in README.

findings.issue: 'Something went wrong' heading string duplicated in shared/load-state.ts:17; a wording change needs two edits and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Export the string (or the heading function) from one module and use it in both.

findings.issue: The presentational card list injects the PokeApi data service to build sprite URLs, coupling it to the data layer.
findings.suggestion: Precompute the sprite URL in CardData (cardsFor already has it) or pass it via a small pure function input, keeping the component purely presentational.

findings.issue: Scroll-restoration behavior is split across app.ts (path changes), home.ts:47-53 (pagination), and pokemon-page.ts:52-63 (fragment jump); debugging scroll issues means three files.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate in the root component (e.g. handle query-only navigations there too), or add a short comment in each file pointing at the others.

findings.issue: Default API origin duplicated in api-config.ts:3 and server/server.mjs:20 (cross-runtime, but a default change needs both).
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but document in server.mjs that api-config.ts holds the browser-side fallback default.

summary: A small, current-Angular-22 app with excellent seams: all data flows through one PokeApi service and pure loader functions, all card lists render through one component, and formatting rules are centralized. The recurring edit friction is duplicated route/resource knowledge between the custom server and the client, and a global stylesheet tied to component selectors. Adding a similar resource page reuses nearly all shared code, with only a thin per-page skeleton to copy.
